title: The wager — twenty thousand at Baring's
learning_goal: Know the fictional trigger, the six names, £20,000 at Baring's, and the deadline; feel the click of a plan.

narration.script: Evening, at the club. Fogg sits down to whist with five fellow members — four hands at the table, the same five every night. In the novel — only in the novel — a thief has robbed the Bank of England of fifty-five thousand pounds. The talk turns to where such a man could hide now. And the Daily Telegraph has done the sums: the world can be crossed in eighty days. That talk becomes a wager. Andrew Stuart, an engineer, bets four thousand pounds it can't be done. Fogg stakes twenty thousand — half his fortune — that it can: 'eighty days or less'. Look at the card: six names, Stuart first, Fogg last. Due back 'in this very room of the Reform Club, on Saturday, the 21st of December, at a quarter before nine p.m.' Exactly eighty days — and it really was a Saturday. Fogg's motto: 'The unforeseen does not exist.' Fogg's bank, Baring's, fell in 1995. The wager has outlived the bank.

variants.clear: Evening, at the club. Fogg plays whist with five fellow members — four hands at the table, the same five men every night. In the story — only in the story — a thief has stolen fifty-five thousand pounds from the Bank of England. Where could such a man hide now? So a newspaper, the Daily Telegraph, counts the days: you can now go around the world in eighty days. At the table this becomes a wager — a bet, with money on it. Andrew Stuart, an engineer, bets four thousand pounds that it cannot be done. Fogg bets twenty thousand pounds — half his money — that it can. Look at the card: six names. Stuart first, Fogg last. Fogg must be back in this same room on Saturday, the twenty-first of December, at a quarter to nine at night. Exactly eighty days. It really was a Saturday. Fogg's motto: 'The unforeseen does not exist.' Fogg's bank, Baring's, failed in 1995. The wager has outlived the bank.

production_notes: The £55,000 theft is Verne's plot device, said as 'in the novel' — never as history. Quotations are Towle's translation and stay inside quotation marks; the plate caption no longer quotes (the words were Stuart's, the plate Neuville's; edition 1873). The six names live on the G-05 card; the guide says 'Stuart first, Fogg last'. A5: 60 → 70 s — the whist arithmetic (five members, four hands) and the reason the robbery is in the scene (where could such a man hide now?) do not fit 60 s at ≤ 2.5 w/s; media windows M-35 0–35, G-05 35–70, M-41 bed 0–70, overlays re-spread. Narrator: ≤ 175 words per track. Linear cut: keep whole (75 s cap, plan 72.3 s), then skip 09 and play 10 without the tap.
